name: start_diagnostics
description:
Start, stop, restart core or plugin services or Open the diagnostic session for a customer-described device/system problem you can't resolve with the normal device/routine/plugin tools -- there's a single diagnostics flow, not a menu of named checks. The response gives you an `instruction` (how to approach diagnosing) and `available_tools` (the steps you can call via run_diagnostic_step) -- read the instruction and follow it; there's no fixed sequence, use judgment based on what the customer described.

Only one diagnostic session can be open at a time, and while one is open, EVERY other tool (not just start_diagnostics/run_diagnostic_step) is refused -- the customer effectively can't do anything else until it concludes, times out, or is stopped, so make sure they understand that before you start one.

Calling start_diagnostics again while a session is already open just re-shows the same instruction/steps -- it does not restart anything. A session left open too long without concluding/stopping is treated as abandoned and cleared automatically, letting a new one start.

candidate_devices.description: **DO NOT USE IF ALL/EVERYTHING IN USER QUERY**. Optional list of devices/groups/scenes that seem relevant to this diagnostic session, with relevance scores -- e.g. for a fuzzy request like "why is my master bathroom scene so intermittent", include every device/scene whose name matches "master bathroom". Carried along as context for what the session concerns (echoed back in every response for it) so it's clear which devices/scenes the customer meant.

device_id.description: The unique device or group/scene identifier

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)

candidate_routines.description: **DO NOT USE IF ALL/EVERYTHING IN USER QUERY**. Optional list of routines/folders that seem relevant to this diagnostic session, with relevance scores -- same idea as candidate_devices but for routines/folders.

score.description: Relevance score from 0.0 to 1.0 inclusive (higher is better)
